items.title: The visual language of warehouse automation
items.clientDescriptor: A warehouse automation company acquired by a Fortune 500 home-improvement retailer
items.problem: A warehouse floor is a negotiation between robots, storage systems, inventory, people and hundreds of services, each speaking its own dialect. At scale, nobody can see the whole conversation at once. The client, a warehouse automation company, needed its floor to be legible: one language that everything on it could speak.
items.solution: We built that language. A visual system that translates what robots, goods-to-person storage, inventory and services are doing into one coherent, live picture, coordinating hundreds of services without asking any of them to change what they are. Architecture first: the language had to survive new robots, new services and new sites without being redesigned.
items.outcome: It survived the hardest test there is: acquisition. A Fortune 500 retailer bought the company after piloting the system in its own distribution network, and now runs it at network scale. The language did not stay a pilot. It became how the floor is read.
items.leftBehind: The visual grammar itself: documented, extensible, and in daily use by teams that never met us.

items.title: Payments that stopped going missing
items.clientDescriptor: US banking software company serving regional and community banks
items.problem: Regional banks run on core systems that predate the processes built on top of them. Between the core and the customer, work passes through hands, queues and integrations, and the worst failures are quiet: transfers that arrive late, records that disagree, transactions that dissolve into reconciliation. Trust erodes one missing payment at a time.
items.solution: We worked inside the client's platform, the layer that orchestrates banking processes end to end on top of those cores, with one standard: delays become guarantees. Deterministic processing, reconciliation that closes instead of accumulating, and transaction security treated as architecture rather than as an audit checkbox.
items.outcome: Payments stopped going missing. Delays became guarantees. Those systems are still standing, years later, untouched by us. That last part is the signature: we build things that do not need us.
items.leftBehind: Systems that run without us. No retainer, no dependency, no signature.
